Alex.confusing: Why my Kookaburra visit in round 1 gave no role info. It was unclear whether I was confused or hugged, and the report didn't say.
Alex.fun: Round 2, when my Hawk egg exposed Finley and the table lined up behind it. Cross-checking the claims against each other worked well.
Alex.change: Show a short note when a night action is blocked or hugged, so players can reason better.
Alex.regret: In round 1 I claimed a Casey visit and said "nobody visited me" without knowing why my report was blank. I'd say less. In rounds 2 and 3 I threw only 3 cards when I could have thrown more to widen my lead over Finley, who finished first.

Blair.confusing: Nothing major, though how the Eagle and Owl visitor lists interact with the Hugged and Confused states took some thought.
Blair.fun: Round 2, when my Eagle report lined up with Alex's Hawk egg and the table converged on Finley quickly. It was satisfying to bank 32 points on one throw.
Blair.change: I would let Meowfia learn at least a hint about their teammates. Round 3 as a lone Sphinx felt nearly unwinnable, because the Farm just cross-checked visitor lists.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I claimed Tit and said I visited Drew, who I knew was the Owl. The Owl's visitor list exposed the lie. I should have claimed a role that couldn't be checked, such as Turkey, or put suspicion on someone else early.

Casey.confusing: How a Floofer's hug interacts with visitor reports. In round 1 I couldn't tell what the hug would show or how others' reports would look, and the table's Floofer theory was hard to judge.
Casey.fun: Round 3: my Kookaburra visit revealed Blair as the Sphinx. The Owl's and Tit's reports then lined up and the table converged on Blair quickly.
Casey.change: Show each player's score standing during the round, not only at its start. I'd also make Meowfia less of a lone guess in round 1, when everyone is Farm-heavy and the cat gets piled on.
Casey.regret: In round 1 I claimed Hawk and named the player I really visited, Drew. That gave the table a checkable story to attack. I'd claim a role that predicts nothing, like Turkey, or stay vague about who I visited.

Drew.confusing: How a Floofer's hug interacts with the Eagle's report in round 1. I couldn't tell whether my zero eggs meant no visitors or that I'd been hugged.
Drew.fun: Round 3, when my Owl report of Kookaburra, Mouser and Tit visiting Blair contradicted Blair's Tit claim. It let the table solve the round quickly.
Drew.change: Make the standings and card values easier to track. The Farm side won every round, so scoring came down to who threw the most cards, which made the game feel less about deduction.
Drew.regret: In round 1 I said four visitors to Casey contradicted my zero eggs, which was muddled. I also kept H2 in round 2, a small mistake. I should have thrown everything each time, since the Farm team was so sure and kept cards are worth only 1 each.

Ellis.confusing: How nest size interacts with scoring: kept cards are worth only 1 each, while thrown cards bank at full value only if your team wins. It wasn't obvious how much to throw in round 1.
Ellis.fun: Round 2 as the Sphinx. Learning that Alex was the real Hawk, then watching the Farm players' reports interlock and take down Finley.
Ellis.change: I'd give Meowfia some way to coordinate or recognize each other. Cats who don't know each other and are outnumbered are very likely to lose, and I lost two rounds in a row as Meowfia.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I stayed silent and never used my Wink. I should have winked Drew, the Owl whose visitor list exposed Blair, and then cast doubt on the other claims. I also threw only one card each in rounds 2 and 3, which left me with a score pile of only 21 points and last place.

Finley.confusing: How the throw payoff works when a team loses. Only your single highest card comes back if you threw at the other team, so a losing throw is costly. I also wasn't sure whether the Mouser's Wink was worth using.
Finley.fun: Round 3. My Tit visit to Blair, plus Drew's Owl report, cleanly exposed the Sphinx. Throwing my whole nest at Blair and finishing first was satisfying.
Finley.change: Give the Meowfia a way to find each other or a bit more night information. As Mouser I learned one role and was then outnumbered by consistent Farm reports, with little to bluff with.
Finley.regret: In round 2, as the Mouser, I never used my Wink. I could have killed Alex, the Hawk accuser, before he got going, which might have broken the chain of Farm reports. Winking early would have been better than saying nothing and losing anyway.

review.title: Leader Gets Piled On
review.headline: Three rounds, three easy cat hunts, and Finley quietly banked the win.
review.summary: Farm won every round. Each time the table converged on one suspect within two beats and eggsecuted a Meowfia. Round 1 was a murky pile-on on Casey, who was a real Floofer. In rounds 2 and 3 night reports (Hawk egg, Owl visitor list, Kookaburra and Sphinx info) exposed the cat quickly. Finley won by throwing everything at correct targets each round, and the Meowfia mostly gave up and threw one card at a Farm player.

rounds.recap: Casey the Floofer hugged Drew and hugged all four visitors, so nobody got any info. Casey claimed Hawk. Drew's Eagle zero looked odd but the table still agreed on Casey as the only odd story. All Farm threw at Casey and won. Finley banked 30.

Ellis (Sphinx) and Finley (Mouser) were the cats and did not know each other. Alex's Hawk egg, Drew's Owl list and Blair's Eagle list all pointed at Finley, who claimed Tit and could not hold it. Ellis stayed quiet and Finley was eggsecuted with a huge Farm throw. Blair took the lead.

Blair (Sphinx) claimed Tit, but Casey's Kookaburra, Drew's Owl list and Finley's real Tit all contradicted it. Blair was eggsecuted in two beats. Ellis (Mouser) held a Wink and never used it. Finley threw all six cards at Blair and jumped to first.

highlights.text: Casey's Floofer hugged all four visitors, so every report was blank and Drew's zero-egg Eagle result clashed with three visit claims.
Alex's Hawk egg, Drew's Owl list and Blair's Eagle list all confirmed each other and pinned Finley within one beat.
Finley, caught, warned the table that the other cat was among them. Ellis, the other cat, stayed silent and survived.
Drew noticed that a Tit visited Blair, so Blair could not be the Tit who visited Drew. That broke the lie.

confusions.what: Claimed Hawk but said Drew isn't Meowfia because nothing happened to Casey. A Hawk only gets an egg if the target is Meowfia, so this was a weak and self-serving inference.
Said Casey's Hawk visit 'should have shown up' on his Eagle count and mixed this up with being hugged. His reasoning was muddled about how visits and hugs interact.
Claimed Tit and said he visited Ellis, but as Mouser he visited Blair. Also said he didn't know why three people hit him, which ignored the Hawk egg.
Claimed Tit with a visit to Drew, but his Sphinx night action was to name Owl, so he never visited anyone. Drew's visitor list showed a Tit had visited Blair.
Held a Wink as Mouser and never used it. He reasoned it would not swing the vote, but he could have killed a key talker.

worked: Visitor-list roles (Owl, Eagle) and the Hawk egg gave checkable, cross-referenced evidence. In rounds 2 and 3 these made the lie visible.
Floofer hugging in round 1 created a real puzzle. Blank reports and a zero-egg Eagle could be read as either honest or a cat's work.
The consolation rule (best card returns if you throw at the other team) gave losing cats a reason to throw at Farm. It cost them nothing.
Public throw counts showed confidence. Finley's six-card throw made the leader obvious to everyone.
problems: Farm won all three rounds in two beats with CAW CAW. Meowfia have no way to cast doubt, and the day ends before they can try. Fix: raise the CAW threshold, or give cats a role that attacks Farm info.

The cats don't know each other and are mostly passive. Ellis and Finley (round 2) and Blair and Ellis (round 3) didn't coordinate, and the cat roles rarely changed the outcome. Fix: give each cat a night action that makes false info, not just reads.
The Mouser's Wink was never used, in either round it was held. It is too weak to act on when the vote is already one-sided. Fix: let a Wink be used after the vote count, or make it worth more.

Scoring rewards the 'safe' play too strongly. All Farm throw their whole nest at the consensus target and bank large totals. Finley won with 70 just by always throwing everything. Fix: cap banked cards per round, or tie the value to uncertainty.

The Farm roles that checked the leader (Owl and Kookaburra in round 3) all visited the score leader, so the cat was exposed by the first night. Cats have no way of hiding when everyone targets the leader. Fix: hide scores, or randomise visits.
